basis.quote: A set of witness-indexed signatures on an interaction, inception, or rotation (delegated or not) for which the effective witness list is not empty MUST satisfy the current witness threshold (of accountable duplicity) for that event to be accepted as valid.
basis.text: Interoperability with keripy 1.x, not conformance: the reading the suite's KERI decision procedure (docs/design.md, KERI) gives a KERI 1.0 body with keripy 1.x's field set, where keri-v1.0.1 would grade the same reading MUST under the quoted sentence. No specification defines the KERI 1.x field sets or the CESR 1.00 attachment codes. keripy 1.2.14 (commit bab95c16e949b61398129a3e41a8f68bad84c94f) is the cross-check (generators/keripy1x_check, generators/DISAGREEMENTS.md).

spec_conflicts.quote: A [[ref: Validator]] that receives a key event or non-key-event message that does not have attached at least one verifiable Controller signature MUST drop that message (i.e., not escrow or otherwise accept it).
spec_conflicts.why: A receipt is a non-key-event message that carries witness signatures, not controller signatures, so read literally this sentence requires every witness receipt to be dropped. That contradicts the same paragraph's completion of a threshold 'to a receipt of that event' and lines 1286 and 1782. The cases apply the drop rule to key events only.

description: The inception of KS-45 with no witness signatures, a receipt from the first witness, and a receipt whose signature, indexed to the second witness, was not made by it. Only one witness signature verifies, so a validator must not accept the inception. Built on keripy 1.x's wire: KERI 1.0 bodies with keripy 1.x's field sets and CESR 1.00 attachments, mirroring KERI-0039 (KS-48) in keri-v1.0.1.
title: keripy 1.x: receipt with a forged witness signature
